$comment: Budgets for the living work-tracking documents. Read by work_tracking/scripts/size-check.js,
which the work-tracking CI job runs as a hard gate. See R-0424 for why this is code rather
than a paragraph: the archive mechanism already existed and simply stopped being applied.
Each budget is a RATCHET, not an aspiration — it is set just above the file's size on
2026-08-09, so a document cannot grow much without someone consciously raising the number in
this file. Raising one is a visible, reviewable act in a diff. That is the whole mechanism.
Two measures, because the two failures this workstream was opened over are invisible to each
other: HANDOFF.md reached 3,396 LINES (R-0417), and PROJECT_PLAN.md reached 4,528 COLUMNS in
a single table cell while its line count looked healthy (R-0423). A line budget alone would
have missed the second; a column budget alone would have missed the first.
Not governed, deliberately: registry.md and registry.db are generated and growing is correct
for them; docs/handoff/archive/** and docs/planning/completed/** are frozen by definition;
records/*.md are one item each and stay small on their own.

documents.remedy: Archive it to docs/handoff/archive/<date>-*.md and cut a fresh one. A narrative belongs in a record, not here — see this file's own closing section.
Move the prose into records and leave a pointer. The column budget is high because the snapshot table pads to its widest cell; if it trips, a cell has become a mega-cell again (R-0423).

documents.was: 312 lines / 100 columns on 2026-08-10, after §3 moved to WORKFLOW.md (R-0441). Budget RATCHETED DOWN from 450, which had been set against the combined document.
documents.remedy: The field reference should track the schema, not accumulate commentary. Reasoning about a schema change is a decision record; anything about operating the store belongs in WORKFLOW.md.

documents.was: 179 lines / 100 columns on 2026-08-10, the day it was split out of SCHEMA.md (R-0441)
documents.remedy: This is the operating manual, not a changelog of how the loop evolved. A new rule that only matters once is a record; a rule that binds every session belongs in AGENTS.md §A with the mechanism here.
This design is settled. New thinking is a new record, not an appendix here.
The phases are fixed. Progress lives in the records the phases name, not in this file.
This is a STUB. Its content is in the registry and HANDOFF.md says not to add entries here. If it grew, someone did anyway — put the item in the registry instead.
This is a STUB. A bug fix is a record with type=bug, not an entry here.
